Thin porcelain shells bonded to the front of your teeth. What they cover is narrow, and it is worth being precise about it.
Chips and cracks
Damage to the visible edge of a tooth, covered rather than patched.
Gaps between teeth
Spacing closed without orthodontics, when the gap is cosmetic rather than structural.
Irregular tooth shape
Teeth that are short, worn, or simply the wrong proportion for your face.
Stains and discolouration
Deep staining that professional whitening cannot lift.

nodes.v: The Straight Answer
When veneers are the wrong choice
A cosmetic dentist who only ever recommends the cosmetic treatment is not worth trusting with your face.
Veneers hide problem areas. They do
not

address functional concerns. If your issue is a missing tooth, a failing tooth, or a bite that is doing damage, a veneer sits on top of an unsolved problem — and Arvada Dental Center will tell you so.

Patients with serious oral health issues such as periodontitis are generally not candidates until that is treated. Where the concern is alignment rather than appearance, Invisalign® or Six Month Smiles is usually the better answer. Where it is function, that is what implants are for.
See dental implants →

attr.alt: Porcelain veneer shells shown against a model of the upper front teeth

nodes.v: Candidacy · three things Dr. Bennett checks first
Gum health
Veneers meet the gum line, so inflammation or periodontal disease has to be resolved first. The practice offers LANAP laser therapy where it is needed.
Decay and structural soundness
A veneer bonds to enamel. Where there is significant decay or a tooth is structurally compromised, a crown is the sounder option.
Bite, grinding and clenching
Porcelain is strong but not indestructible. If you grind, that gets addressed as part of the plan rather than discovered afterwards.

nodes.v: The Design
Three decisions, made with you

The design is worked out against your facial features, skin tone and gum line rather than a catalogue shade. Shade, shape and proportion are decided with you — which is the whole answer to "will they look obviously fake".
Shade
Translucency matched to real enamel, not a flat white. Porcelain holds that colour rather than picking up stain.
Shape
Worn, chipped and short teeth are given an edge and a contour that suits your face.
Proportion
Widths and spacing are set together, so gaps close without the result looking like a row of tiles.
Illustration of the decisions, not a photograph and not a simulation of your result. What is achievable for your teeth is settled at the evaluation.

nodes.v: The Method
Two visits, one design.
Visit one
Preparation and design

Dr. Bennett removes a small portion of enamel from the front of the teeth being treated, and the design is worked out against your facial features, skin tone and gum line rather than a catalogue shade.
Between
Made to fit you
The practice's own technology handles the design, and the veneers are fabricated for your case rather than picked from a tray.
Visit two
Fitted and bonded
The finished veneers go on. Veneers can be combined with laser gum surgery where the gum line itself is part of the problem — a full smile makeover rather than a set of shells.
In the room
CEREC & digital X-rays
Digital impressions instead of a tray of setting putty — considerably more pleasant if you have a gag reflex — and full-mouth panoramic imaging at a fraction of the radiation of film.
In the room
Waterlase & IV sedation
Gentle laser work on soft tissue makes combining veneers with gum contouring practical, and Dr. Bennett is board certified to administer IV sedation himself.

nodes.v: The Materials
Not all veneers are the same thing
"Veneer" covers two quite different treatments. The difference shows up years later, which is exactly when it is hardest to undo.

Composite veneers compared with the porcelain veneers used at Arvada Dental Center
  Composite / traditional Porcelain, minimal-prep
Appearance in daylightMore opaque — can read flatTranslucency matched to real enamel
Tooth preparationOften more enamel removedMinimal-prep, tooth-conserving
StainingPicks up stain over timeHighly stain-resistant
Visits to completeVaries, often repeat touch-upsAs few as two
Typical service life†Around 4–8 years10–20+ years with proper care

nodes.v: A written plan and price before you commit to anything
Book my smile evaluation
Veneer fees depend on the number of teeth treated and are quoted in writing after examination. Monthly payment plans are available; HMO and Medicaid plans are not accepted.
Before you commit
<button aria-controls="vnr-vq1" aria-expanded="false" class="vnr-faq__q">How many visits does it take?</button>

meta.html: <button aria-controls="vnr-vq1" aria-expanded="false" class="vnr-faq__q">How many visits does it take?</button>

nodes.v: As few as two. The first prepares the teeth and settles the design; the second fits the finished veneers.
<button aria-controls="vnr-vq2" aria-expanded="false" class="vnr-faq__q">Will they look obviously fake?</button>

meta.html: <button aria-controls="vnr-vq2" aria-expanded="false" class="vnr-faq__q">Will they look obviously fake?</button>

nodes.v: That is a design question rather than a materials one. The practice designs each case against your facial features, skin tone and gum line — which is exactly why the shade, shape and proportion are decided with you rather than off a chart.
<button aria-controls="vnr-vq3" aria-expanded="false" class="vnr-faq__q">Is enamel really removed?</button>

meta.html: <button aria-controls="vnr-vq3" aria-expanded="false" class="vnr-faq__q">Is enamel really removed?</button>

nodes.v: Yes — a small portion from the front of each treated tooth, so the veneer sits flush rather than proud. It is not reversible, which is why the candidacy checks above happen first.
<button aria-controls="vnr-vq6" aria-expanded="false" class="vnr-faq__q">What's the difference between porcelain veneers and composite bonding?</button>

meta.html: <button aria-controls="vnr-vq6" aria-expanded="false" class="vnr-faq__q">What's the difference between porcelain veneers and composite bonding?</button>

nodes.v: Bonding is resin shaped onto the tooth in the chair — quicker and cheaper, but more opaque, more prone to staining, and shorter-lived. Porcelain is made to fit you and holds its colour. For a single small chip, bonding is often the sensible answer; for a smile you want to stop thinking about, it usually isn't. See the comparison above.
<button aria-controls="vnr-vq4" aria-expanded="false" class="vnr-faq__q">What if I want straighter teeth, not covered ones?</button>

meta.html: <button aria-controls="vnr-vq4" aria-expanded="false" class="vnr-faq__q">What if I want straighter teeth, not covered ones?</button>

nodes.v: Then say so at the evaluation. The practice offers Invisalign® and Six Month Smiles, and for misalignment those are usually the better answer.
<button aria-controls="vnr-vq5" aria-expanded="false" class="vnr-faq__q">What will it cost?</button>

meta.html: <button aria-controls="vnr-vq5" aria-expanded="false" class="vnr-faq__q">What will it cost?</button>

nodes.v: It depends entirely on how many teeth are treated, so the practice quotes in writing after examining you rather than publishing a per-tooth figure. Monthly payment plans are available if you would rather spread the cost.
